// Names identified by hand, at their addresses in init (us.v11).
//
// tools/gen_symbols.py finds every copy of these functions in every module and
// version (same instructions once addresses are masked) and names each copy,
// along with the globals the copy uses in place of the ones named here.  The
// text after `//` becomes the tag in the generated files.
//
// Rare's gzip decompressor, from gzip 1.2.4.  init uses it to inflate hd_code,
// and hd_code has its own copy for hd_front_end.  The evidence for each name:
//   inflate         wp = bk = bb = 0; inflate_block() until e; give back
//                   whole bytes of lookahead (while (bk >= 8) inptr--).  Rare
//                   adds inptr += 8 to skip the gzip trailer.
//   inflate_block   1 bit e, 2 bits t: 2 dynamic, 0 stored, 1 fixed, else 2.
//   inflate_stored  aligns to a byte, reads n, copies n bytes (Rare dropped
//                   the ~n check).
//   inflate_fixed   lengths 8/9/7/8 up to 144/256/280/288, huft_build(l, 288,
//                   257, cplens, cplext, ...), then 30 distances of length 5.
//   inflate_dynamic border[19], lbits/dbits, all four tables, huft_build.
//   huft_build      BMAX 16, invalid-code marker 99.  No huft_free: Rare
//                   allocates the tables from a static heap.
//   inflate_codes   mask_bits, e > 16 extra-bits handling.
//   get_method      method byte must be 8, else "kiunzip: unknown method %d --
//                   get newer version of gzip" and exit_code = 1; then skips
//                   the header fields by flag; header_bytes = inptr + 8.
//   clear_bufs      outcnt = 0; insize = inptr = 0; bytes_in = bytes_out = 0,
//                   stored in that order, which is what tells the globals apart.
//   bi_reverse      exactly gzip's bits.c version.
//   huft_heap       where huft_build takes its tables from, in place of
//                   malloc: q = huft_heap + hufts, then hufts += z + 1.
//                   func_80220360 sets it from its third argument.
// outcnt is inflate's wp (gzip: #define wp outcnt); window is where inflate
// writes, which Rare points straight at the destination.  The table contents
// (cplens 3..258, mask_bits 0..0xFFFF, border 16,17,18,0,8,...) and lbits = 9,
// dbits = 6 are gzip's.

huft_build = 0x8021ED50; // type:func gzip
inflate_codes = 0x8021F3EC; // type:func gzip
inflate_stored = 0x8021F7F4; // type:func gzip
inflate_fixed = 0x8021F988; // type:func gzip
inflate_dynamic = 0x8021FB30; // type:func gzip
inflate_block = 0x8022011C; // type:func gzip
inflate = 0x80220268; // type:func gzip
get_method = 0x8022043C; // type:func gzip
bi_reverse = 0x8022069C; // type:func gzip
clear_bufs = 0x802206D0; // type:func gzip

border = 0x80222740; // type:data gzip
cplens = 0x80222754; // type:data gzip
cplext = 0x80222794; // type:data gzip
cpdist = 0x802227B4; // type:data gzip
cpdext = 0x802227F0; // type:data gzip
mask_bits = 0x80222810; // type:data gzip
lbits = 0x80222834; // type:data gzip
dbits = 0x80222838; // type:data gzip
method = 0x80222840; // type:data gzip
exit_code = 0x80222844; // type:data gzip
huft_heap = 0x802229E0; // type:data gzip
bb = 0x802229E4; // type:data gzip
bk = 0x802229E8; // type:data gzip
hufts = 0x802229EC; // type:data gzip
inbuf = 0x802229F0; // type:data gzip
window = 0x802229F4; // type:data gzip
header_bytes = 0x802229FC; // type:data gzip
bytes_in = 0x80222A08; // type:data gzip
bytes_out = 0x80222A0C; // type:data gzip
insize = 0x80222A18; // type:data gzip
inptr = 0x80222A1C; // type:data gzip
outcnt = 0x80222A20; // type:data gzip

// libultra functions tools/libmatch.py can't place: this libultra is older
// than any ultralib builds, and these changed since.
//   osInitialize    ultralib's pre-2.0J initialize.c without the osViClock
//                   part: __osFinalrom = 1, SR |= CU1, FPCSR 0x01000800, PIF
//                   RAM 0x1FC007FC |= 8, __osExceptionPreamble copied to the
//                   four vectors, osMapTLBRdb, clock rate from ROM header
//                   offset 4 then * 3 / 4, bzero(osAppNMIBuffer, 0x40) when
//                   osResetType is 0.
//   osDestroyThread dequeues t (t = __osRunningThread if NULL) unless it's
//                   stopped, unlinks it from __osActiveQueue by tlnext, and
//                   dispatches if it was running.  ultralib's destroythread.c.
//   osSetIntMask    setintmask.s: mfc0 SR, MI_INTR_MASK << 16, the
//                   __osRcpImTable lookup by (mask & 0x3F0000) >> 15.
//   __osException   exceptasm.s: __osExceptionPreamble jumps to it
//                   (lui/addiu k0, jr k0).  Named here so its globals,
//                   __osRdbSendMessage and __osFaultedThread, get names too.
//                   Its pre-NMI path tests __osShutdown (initialize.c's
//                   second variable, after osClockRate); hardware interrupts
//                   dispatch through __osHwIntTable (lw at table + 4 * n).
// kdebugserver.c in its 2.0D-era form, as in SM64's libultra: the state
// machine on debugState/numChars/numCharsToReceive, command 1 sends memory
// (address and length as big-endian u32s at debugBuffer + 1 and + 5),
// command 2 sends __osThreadSave.context (0x190 bytes, the size of
// __OSThreadContext, from offset 0x20 of an OSThread).  send() waits for IP6
// once when __osRdbWriteOK is 0, then sends in packets of 3.

osInitialize = 0x80220C40; // type:func libultra
__osException = 0x80221040; // type:func libultra
u32_to_string = 0x80221E10; // type:func libultra
string_to_u32 = 0x80221E40; // type:func libultra
send_packet = 0x80221E98; // type:func libultra
send = 0x80221F58; // type:func libultra
process_command_memory = 0x80222030; // type:func libultra
process_command_register = 0x8022207C; // type:func libultra
kdebugserver = 0x802220A8; // type:func libultra
osSetIntMask = 0x80222470; // type:func libultra
osDestroyThread = 0x802224D0; // type:func libultra

osClockRate = 0x80222860; // type:data libultra
__osShutdown = 0x80222868; // type:data libultra
__osHwIntTable = 0x80222870; // type:data libultra
debugState = 0x80222890; // type:data libultra
numChars = 0x80222894; // type:data libultra
numCharsToReceive = 0x80222898; // type:data libultra
__osActiveQueue = 0x802228AC; // type:data libultra
__osRunningThread = 0x802228B0; // type:data libultra
__osFaultedThread = 0x802228B4; // type:data libultra
__osRdbSendMessage = 0x802228C0; // type:data libultra
__osRdbWriteOK = 0x802228C4; // type:data libultra
__osRcpImTable = 0x80222960; // type:data libultra
__osFinalrom = 0x80224A40; // type:data libultra
debugBuffer = 0x80224A50; // type:data libultra
__osThreadSave = 0x80224B50; // type:data libultra
osResetType = 0x8000030C; // type:data libultra
osAppNMIBuffer = 0x8000031C; // type:data libultra

// libultra in hd_code (us.v11 hd_code addresses), identified while writing
// their C from ultralib's source (see blastcorps/src/libultra/): each one
// matches the named source function, and is where its callers and data say.
//   osContInit etc.   controller.c/contreaddata.c: PIF request building and
//                     __osContPifRam use.
//   osCreatePiManager / osCreateViManager / viMgrMain / __osDevMgrMain:
//                     create the PI/VI manager threads and message queues
//                     (__osPiDevMgr, __osViDevMgr); the loops dispatch on
//                     OS_MESG_TYPE_*.
//   The alCSP* setters/getters: each sends or reads the event/field of
//                     ALCSPlayer that libaudio's cspsetxxx.c does (vol at
//                     0x32, state at 0x2C).  alSeqp* compiles the same; these
//                     are CSP because their callers use alCSPNew/alCSPGetTempo.
osCreatePiManager = 0x802D4560; // type:func libultra
alCSPGetState = 0x802D4E10; // type:func libultra
proutSprintf = 0x802D6ACC; // type:func libultra
alCSPSetSeq = 0x802D81B0; // type:func libultra
alCSPPlay = 0x802D81F0; // type:func libultra
alCSPSetVol = 0x802D8220; // type:func libultra
alCSPSetTempo = 0x802D82A0; // type:func libultra
alCSPGetVol = 0x802D8310; // type:func libultra
_bnkfPatchBank = 0x802D8370; // type:func libultra
alCSPSetBank = 0x802D97E0; // type:func libultra
__osViInit = 0x802D98D0; // type:func libultra
osAiSetNextBuffer = 0x802D9B60; // type:func libultra
osCreateViManager = 0x802DA610; // type:func libultra
viMgrMain = 0x802DA794; // type:func libultra
_VirtualToPhysicalTask = 0x802DAD00; // type:func libultra
osContInit = 0x802DB0A0; // type:func libultra
osContStartReadData = 0x802DB4D0; // type:func libultra
osContGetReadData = 0x802DB594; // type:func libultra
__osPackReadData = 0x802DB63C; // type:func libultra
__osDevMgrMain = 0x802DC570; // type:func libultra
_Putfld = 0x802DD3DC; // type:func libultra
_decodeChunk = 0x802E0B20; // type:func libultra
_Ldunscale = 0x802E37C0; // type:func libultra

// libultra in hd_front_end (us.v11 hd_front_end addresses): the Controller

osEepromProbe = 0x80202880; // type:func libultra

__osClearPage = 0x80203BF8; // type:func libultra

__osPfsGetNextPage = 0x80204710; // type:func libultra

__osPackEepWriteData = 0x80204DC0; // type:func libultra
__osEepStatus = 0x80204ECC; // type:func libultra
osEepromRead = 0x802050F0; // type:func libultra
__osPackEepReadData = 0x802052E0; // type:func libultra

// The scheduler (us.v11 hd_code addresses): hd_code 2C560.c, "sched.c" in its
// asserts, is Rare's version of SGI's sample scheduler (sched.c/sched.h, the
// asserts quote its field names).  libmatch.py places osScRemoveClient, which
// Rare left alone; these changed, and are named by SGI's function each one is:
//   osCreateScheduler  (sc, stack, priority, mode, numFields): the two message
//                      queues, osCreateViManager, osViSetMode, the SP/DP/PRENMI/
//                      FAULT event messages and osViSetEvent on interruptQ,
//                      then the thread on __scMain.
//   osScAddClient      links c into sc->clientList under osSetIntMask(
//                      OS_IM_NONE), as SGI's; Rare added two client fields.
//   osScGetCmdQ        returns &sc->cmdQ.  audio.c's assert "osSendMesg(
//                      osScGetCmdQ(&sc), (OSMesg) t, OS_MESG_NOBLOCK)!=-1" sits
//                      on its call.
//   __scMain           the thread: osRecvMesg(&sc->interruptQ), a switch on the
//                      message, sending tasks on to be scheduled.
//   __scHandleRetrace  the retrace message: frameCount++, the cmdQ drain with
//                      "osRecvMesg(&sc->cmdQ, (OSMesg *)&rspTask, ...) != -1".
//   __scHandleRSP      the SP message: "sc->curRSPTask", the yield case, then
//                      __scTaskComplete.
//   __scHandleRDP      the DP message: "sc->curRDPTask", the buffer swap.
//   __scTaskComplete   (flags & 3) == ((flags >> 2) & 3), unlinks a finished
//                      gfx task, replies on t->msgQ ("rv!=-1").
//   __scAppendList     "(type == M_AUDTASK) || (type == M_GFXTASK)", appends to
//                      the audio or gfx list.
//   __scYield          "sc->curRSPTask->list.t.type != M_AUDTASK", "...->state
//                      != RSP_STATE_SUSPENDED", osSpTaskYield.
osCreateScheduler = 0x80270D20; // type:func sched
osScAddClient = 0x80270E50; // type:func sched
osScGetCmdQ = 0x80270F74; // type:func sched
__scMain = 0x80270F7C; // type:func sched
__scHandleRetrace = 0x80271358; // type:func sched
__scHandleRSP = 0x802715DC; // type:func sched
__scHandleRDP = 0x80271904; // type:func sched
__scTaskComplete = 0x80271A84; // type:func sched
__scAppendList = 0x80271C24; // type:func sched
__scYield = 0x80271E88; // type:func sched
